title: Snapshot-based cohort comparator and trace-linked diff view for rollouts
creator: Marco Rodriguez
description:
Objective: Build a snapshot-based comparator and trace-linked diff view in the Console to help engineers quickly evaluate behavioral and quality differences across rollout cohorts (canary, A/B arms, and shadow traffic) and make observable-driven rollout decisions (promote, hold, rollback).

Scope:
- Capture consistent per-route snapshots for configured cohorts at configurable intervals (e.g., first-hour, 24-hour, 7-day) and store lightweight diffs for fast rendering.
- Provide side-by-side metric diffs (latency p50/p95, token cost, error rates, hallucination rate proxies, output length distributions) and per-route histograms.
- Enable trace linking: from any metric delta or individual request sampled in a snapshot, jump to the request trace (distributed trace view) with model input/response, tokens, and model variant metadata.
- Support rollouts types: canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic comparisons.
- Integrate with auto-rollback: surface alert suggestions and one-click rollback triggers tied to configured SLO breaches and model-variant fallback policies.
- UI must work at per-route and account levels and allow time-window comparison and cohort rebaselining.

User stories:
- As an engineer running a 10% canary, I want to see a compact diff summary showing p95 latency, error rate, and quality regressions after 3 hours so I can decide whether to promote.
- As a PM running an A/B experiment, I want to compare model outputs for the same seed prompts across cohorts and sample traces where outputs diverge.
- As an SRE, I want automatic rollback suggestions when a canary breaches error-rate thresholds and a quick path to roll the canary back to the previous model variant.

Telemetry surface:
- Metrics to compare: request count, success rate, server and end-to-end latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), tokens per request, cost per token, model confidence proxies (where available), rerank delta, prompt truncation counts, hallucination proxy (semantic similarity to ground truth prompts when available), and user-facing error types.
- Sampling: high-cardinality tracing must be sampled; proposal: deterministic head-sampling for first N requests per route per cohort + probabilistic tail sampling for outliers.
- Snapshot retention: store full snapshot diffs for 30 days, aggregated deltas for 90 days. Provide export API for longer retention.

Deliverables:
- Console UI: "Comparator" pane under Rollouts with cohort selector, metric summary, detailed per-route diffs, and request-level trace links.
- Backend snapshot service: lightweight snapshot writer and diff store, query API for Console.
- Alerting/auto-rollback integration and runbook templates.
- Documentation and example playbooks (canary thresholds, A/B metric tuning).

Out of scope for this ticket: model evaluation suite (we'll link to Optimize), in-console full-text output diffs for non-deterministic models beyond sampling, long-term archival beyond export API.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Comparator pane renders for a rollout with at least two cohorts and shows metric deltas for p50/p95 latency, error rate, tokens per request, and cost per request.
2) Clicking a row in the per-route table opens a request sample list for the cohort and at least one sample links to the trace viewer with model variant and request metadata.
3) Snapshot diff API responds under 500ms for 95th percentile queries for 30k requests snapshot.
4) Auto-rollback suggestion appears in the Console when configured SLO thresholds are breached and triggers a safe rollback action (requires confirmation).
5) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with example thresholds and playbook steps.
decisions:
- Snapshot vs live-first diff: we decided to adopt periodic snapshots (5m / 1h configurable) to avoid expensive cross-cohort streaming joins in the Console and to provide reproducible comparison points.
- Storage format: store aggregated metric buckets + N request-level samples per bucket (not full request logs) to control storage costs.
- Sampling policy: deterministic head-sampling plus probabilistic tail-sampling to capture regressions and outliers without high ingestion cost.
- Rollback UX: one-click rollback is gated behind a confirmation modal and feature flag; only authorized users (RBAC) may trigger rollback.
- Alerting: initial release will emit suggested alerts; fully automated rollback (no-human) deferred to a follow-up change where stricter safety checks exist.
notes:
2025-02-18 - Marco Rodriguez: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence (link below). Agreed on snapshot cadence defaults: 5m for high-traffic routes, 1h for low-traffic.
2025-02-24 - Evelyn Chen: Wireframes V1 reviewed with UX. Feedback: surface a compact delta sparkline column and ensure comparison time windows are easily swapped.
2025-02-27 - Priya Nair (Eng): Backend proto for snapshot API merged: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-telemetry/pull/314. Needs perf testing on stage with synthetic 50k req/s snapshot.
2025-03-02 - QA plan drafted (link below) and feature-flag toggled in staging. First manual smoke passed for a simple canary.
2025-03-04 - Design signoff received pending follow-up on mobile layout and accessibility adjustments.

Review feedback and follow-ups:
- UX requested inline examples for non-technical PMs; add a toggle to show human-readable summaries.
- Security requested a review of PII propagation in traces; Eng to redact prompt text by default and provide an opt-in full-text link subject to KMS policy.

Next steps: finalize sampling thresholds, run stage load test, and schedule a canary run with internal customers for feedback.
